source: SEP (Bayesian Epistemology) definition of conditionalization
finding: Conditionalization on evidence E sets credence in every possibility that conflicts with E to zero and rescales the rest to sum to 1.
numbers: Cr'(X) = Cr(X and E) / Cr(E), defined only if Cr(E) is not 0. It preserves ratios of credences among the possibilities that survive.
quote: The essence of conditionalization is preservation of certain ratios of credences
limits: Needs E to be learned with certainty and nothing stronger. Undefined for zero-credence evidence under the ratio formula.
agent_relevance: This is the exact operation of S7 and G5: drop what a check rules out, renormalise the survivors in code. Survivors keep their relative odds.

source: SEP (Bayesian Epistemology) history: Bayes, Ramsey, de Finetti
finding: Bayes (1763) is credited with the core ideas. Earman argues the view is Bayesian because the essay holds Probabilism and conditionalization, not because of the theorem. Ramsey (1926) and de Finetti (1937) gave the Dutch Book argument for probabilism.
numbers: SEP example: credences .75 in A and .30 in not-A can be booked for a sure loss of $5.
limits: Dutch Book premise links credence to betting price. Critics say it gives a practical, not epistemic, reason.
agent_relevance: Coherence (credences sum to 1 over exclusive answers) has a long rationale. Incoherent stated probabilities are a known defect to fix in code.

source: SEP Dutch Book Arguments, section 4.1: diachronic Dutch strategy (Teller 1973; Lewis 1999)
finding: If an agent plans to adopt Pr2(A) different from Pr1(A given E) after learning E, a bookie sells four bets and wins a sure amount.
numbers: Sure loss to the agent = [Pr1(A|E) - Pr2(A)] x Pr1(E), in both the E-true and E-false cases. Skyrms (1987) proved a converse: conditionalizers cannot be booked this way.
limits: Van Fraassen (1989): assumes the agent fixes the update rule in advance. Gallow (2019): fails if possible evidence propositions overlap rather than partition. Briggs and Mahtani: shows tension, maybe not strict irrationality.
agent_relevance: Fix the update rule before seeing the check result, so the agent cannot be exploited by its own ad hoc revisions.

source: SEP Dutch Book: null-probability evidence and rigidity complaints
finding: Rescorla (2019) extends the Dutch Book theorem and converse to Kolmogorov conditionalization, which handles evidence with prior probability zero. Levi and Kyburg complain the invariance condition demands unreasonable rigidity of belief.
numbers: Qualitative; proofs are in Rescorla 2019.
limits: Page does not give Levi's objection in detail.
agent_relevance: A candidate at exactly 0 can never come back. Keep a small floor so one wrong check cannot kill the true answer.

source: SEP Bayesian Epistemology section 1.7: accuracy arguments
finding: Credences are treated as estimates of truth values. Non-probabilistic credences are accuracy-dominated (Joyce 1998). Briggs and Pettigrew (2020) extend this to conditionalization as the plan that avoids dominance.
numbers: Qualitative. The SEP extract did not mention Greaves and Wallace (2006), who show conditionalization maximises expected accuracy.
limits: Plan version only: it justifies the plan, not every later revision.
agent_relevance: An accuracy reason, not a betting reason, to normalise: coherent distributions score better on a proper scoring rule.

source: SEP Bayesian Epistemology section 5.3: Jeffrey conditionalization
finding: When evidence is uncertain, scale credences inside and outside E by common factors so the new credence in E is what the experience fixed. No credence is forced to zero.
numbers: Ratios inside E and inside not-E are kept (rigidity). Defended by a Dutch Book argument. Weisberg's Red Jelly Bean case: still too inflexible.
quote: it preserves the credence ratios of the possibilities inside new evidence
limits: Needs the shifted credence in E as input, which the evidence itself does not give.
agent_relevance: A noisy check should shift, not zero, a candidate (links to the Uncertain evidence subfield). Conditionalization is the limit case of a perfect check.

source: SEP Bayesian Epistemology sections 1.5, 3.3, 3.4: priors and zero probabilities
finding: Probabilism plus conditionalization do not fix induction; the verdict depends on the prior. Conditionalizing on a zero-credence proposition is undefined. Regularity (no zero credence for possible events) conflicts with the coin case.
numbers: Responses: infinitesimal credences, comparative probability, Kolmogorov limits.
limits: Unsettled in philosophy.
agent_relevance: The agent needs an explicit prior over candidates (uniform is a default) and a floor above zero.

source: SEP Bayesian Epistemology sections 5.1, 5.2, 5.4, 5.5: known failures
finding: Conditionalization fails or is silent on: old evidence (Mercury and general relativity), new theory (credence drop with no new evidence), memory loss (it preserves certainties), and self-locating belief (Sleeping Beauty: Lewis says 1/2, Elga says 1/3).
numbers: Qualitative.
limits: Open problems, not resolved.
agent_relevance: Problem of new theory maps to our case: if the true answer was never in the candidate set, conditionalizing cannot add it. Generation (S3) and harvesting (S4) must widen the set.

source: Edwards (1968) conservatism, as described on Wikipedia 'Conservatism (belief revision)'
finding: People revise too little after evidence. Bookbag task: bags of 700 red/300 blue vs 300 red/700 blue. Sample with replacement gives 8 red and 4 blue.
numbers: Typical answer about .70. Bayes answer about .97 (0.967). Start .5. People move about 43 percent as far as Bayes.
limits: Secondary page, flagged for relying on primary sources; it did not give Phillips and Edwards 1966 numbers.
agent_relevance: Humans, and LLM text trained on them, under-update on strong evidence. A code-run update would not share this bias.

source: Explanations of conservatism (Hilbert 2012; Oechssler 2009), via Wikipedia page
finding: Competing explanations: anchoring on the prior (Tversky and Kahneman), noisy memory retrieval (Hilbert 2012), and cognitive ability.
numbers: Hilbert example: objective probability 1 becomes 0.727 from memory, smoothed to 0.636. Oechssler et al. 2009 incentivised study: bias shrinks with higher cognitive ability but does not vanish.
limits: Secondary-source summary.
agent_relevance: Under-updating has several causes, so a prompt reminder alone may not remove it.

source: Wikipedia 'Base rate fallacy': Kahneman and Tversky GPA study; frequency formats
finding: Students given descriptive information about a person tended to ignore the statistical distribution. Frequency formats help Bayesian reasoning (Gigerenzer and Hoffrage 1995; Hoffrage 2000; Sedlmeier and Gigerenzer 2001).
numbers: Worked frequency example: 1 in 1000 drivers drunk, 50 of 999 sober flagged, so P(drunk given flagged) = 1/51, about 2 percent.
limits: No effect sizes on the page. Replications cited by name only.
agent_relevance: The opposite error to conservatism: overweighting a vivid case. Giving the model counts, not percentages, is a plausible aid.

source: Kahneman and Tversky (1973) On the psychology of prediction (engineer and lawyer problem)
finding: Subjects judged whether a described person was an engineer or lawyer. Judgments followed similarity to the stereotype, not the stated base rate.
numbers: From memory, NOT opened: groups told 30 vs 70 percent engineers gave nearly the same probabilities; for a null description they judged about 50 percent in both.
limits: Not opened this session. Boundary: base rates are used more when causally relevant (Ajzen 1977; Bar-Hillel 1980).
agent_relevance: Base-rate neglect is the rival failure mode to conservatism. Verify numbers before use.

source: Bar-Hillel (1980) The base-rate fallacy in probability judgments (taxi problem)
finding: Witness 80 percent reliable, 15 percent of cabs are the named colour. Most people answer 80 percent.
numbers: From memory, NOT opened: Bayes answer 41 percent.
limits: Not opened this session.
agent_relevance: Shows the prior-versus-likelihood weighting problem that a code-run Bayes step avoids.

source: Casscells, Schoenberger, Graboys (1978) Harvard staff test problem
finding: Test with 5 percent false positives, prevalence 1 in 1000. Most staff and students did not give the Bayes answer.
numbers: From memory, NOT opened: 11 of 60 gave about 2 percent; many said 95 percent.
limits: Not opened this session.
agent_relevance: Likelihood reasoning in prose is hard even for experts.

source: Gigerenzer and Hoffrage (1995) How to improve Bayesian reasoning without instruction
finding: Natural frequencies raise correct Bayesian answers compared with probabilities.
numbers: From memory, NOT opened: about 16 percent correct with probabilities vs about 46 percent with natural frequencies, averaged over 15 problems.
limits: Not opened. Disputed: Barbey and Sloman (2007) argue nested sets, not frequencies, drive the gain.
agent_relevance: If the model must do Bayes in prose, pass counts. Better to do it in code.

source: Qiu et al. (2025, v3 2026) Bayesian Teaching Enables Probabilistic Reasoning in LLMs: baseline LLMs
finding: LLMs interacting for five rounds with a simulated flight-booking user barely improve after round one. They fall far short of the normative Bayesian Assistant.
numbers: 624 possible users, 3 flights per round, 100 new test sets per round. Bayesian Assistant final-round accuracy 81 percent. Off-the-shelf models in Fig. 2 score about 36 to 58 percent in the final round. 48 humans improved (p = .002) but also fell short of Bayes.
limits: Task is preference inference with a finite hypothesis set, a clean fit for Bayes. Chain-of-thought, numeric formatting, 30 rounds, and pretrain-only models did not help (Appendix C.1).
agent_relevance: Direct evidence that in-context updating plateaus. Keep the belief update in code with a stated likelihood.

source: Qiu et al. 2025 Bayesian teaching: fine-tuning results
finding: Fine-tuning Gemma 2 9B, Llama 3 8B, Qwen 2.5 7B on a Bayesian Assistant's guesses beats fine-tuning on a perfect oracle's answers.
numbers: 10 five-round interactions per user for training. Bayesian-tuned models agree with the Bayesian Assistant about 80 percent of the time, more than original or oracle-tuned. Accuracy keeps rising over rounds. All p < .001. Uniform prior; other priors similar.
limits: Fine-tuning is outside our no-training constraint. For Qwen, belief-based accuracy did not improve even though direct accuracy did.
agent_relevance: Bayes-consistent behaviour is learnable but absent by default. For us: keep the update outside the model.

source: Qiu et al. 2025 Bayesian teaching: generalization
finding: Bayesian-taught models generalise to more features, a hotel domain, a web-shopping domain, and to real human users.
numbers: Per-domain numbers are in Figs. 5 and 6 and were not extracted. Human-user accuracy is lower than simulated users.
limits: Authors attribute the human-user gap to noisy human preferences.
agent_relevance: Skill transfers only after training; no training here.

source: Falck, Wang, Holmes (2024) Is In-Context Learning in LLMs Bayesian? A Martingale Perspective (ICML)
finding: A Bayesian learner on exchangeable data must satisfy the martingale property: its prediction should not depend on order or on imputed missing data. Tested LLMs violate it, more so over long sampling horizons.
numbers: Bernoulli runs: n = 50, path length m = n/2 and 2n, true mean .3, .5, .7, reference Beta(1,1) posterior with 95 percent CI. Short paths mostly inside the CI (gpt-4 an exception for some means); long paths deviate more. gpt-3.5 Gaussian sample variance 0.711, 95 percent CI [0.680, 0.742], below the likelihood variance of 1, which no Bayesian posterior allows.
quote: falsifying the hypothesis that ICL is Bayesian
limits: Models: GPT-3 170B, GPT-3.5, GPT-4 (Bernoulli only), Llama-2-7B, Mistral-7B. Synthetic tasks. Instruction-tuned models were not closer to Bayesian than gpt-3.
agent_relevance: The model's implicit updating is order-dependent and incoherent. Supports G5: select in code, not by model-stated beliefs.

source: Falck et al. 2024: uncertainty scaling and natural-language case
finding: Uncertainty in LLMs does not shrink with more data the way a Bayesian posterior does. Violations also appear when the data are in words (n = 80, m = 40, gpt-3.5 and gpt-4).
numbers: Scaling statistic T3 vs reference Bayes (Fig. 6). Fine-tuned gpt-3-2.7b on 10^4 Bernoulli sequences and 5000 NLP sequences also checked.
limits: Uncertainty figures read as text claims, not as exact numbers.
agent_relevance: Do not read stated confidence as a posterior that sharpens with evidence.

source: Xie, Raventos, Wu, Ma, Liang (2022) An Explanation of In-context Learning as Implicit Bayesian Inference (ICLR)
finding: If pretraining text is a mixture of latent concepts (HMM mixture), a prompt lets the model infer the concept implicitly, which is Bayesian inference over the concept.
numbers: On synthetic GINC, in-context accuracy rises with number of examples n and example length k. Layers 12 to 16 raise accuracy 81 to 85 percent at similar pretraining loss. Order of the same 4 examples changes accuracy by 10 to 40 percent between permutations.
limits: Theory under assumptions on the pretraining distribution; synthetic data. The order sensitivity is non-Bayesian, as Falck et al. press.
agent_relevance: A prompt acts like evidence, but order effects mean: shuffle and aggregate.

source: Zhu and Griffiths (2024) Eliciting the Priors of LLMs using Iterated In-Context Learning
finding: Iterated learning with Bayesian learners converges to the learner's prior. Applied to GPT-4 it recovers priors that match human priors in causal learning, proportion estimation and everyday quantity prediction.
numbers: GPT-4 priors explain GPT-4 decisions better than a uniform prior in those settings. Also elicited priors for speculative events (Mars colony, timing of superhuman AI).
limits: Assumes ICL is Bayesian, which Falck et al. dispute. Per-task numbers not extracted.
agent_relevance: The prior over candidates can be elicited and inspected instead of assumed uniform. Treat as a hypothesis.

source: Zheng et al. (2024) LLMs are not robust multiple choice selectors (ICLR)
finding: Models put prior probability mass on specific option labels such as A. This is a prior bias on the label token, not on content.
numbers: MMLU 0-shot: moving the gold answer to D cuts gpt-3.5-turbo from 67.2 to 60.9. Moving gold to A lifts llama-30B from 53.1 to 68.2. With 250 gold answers each at A to D, llama-30B picks A/B/C/D 34.6/27.3/22.3/15.8 percent. PriDe estimates the prior from about 5 percent of samples by permuting options.
limits: 20 LLMs, 3 benchmarks. Explicit debiasing instructions helped little (Table 2).
agent_relevance: A normalised distribution over exclusive answers needs label-position debiasing: permute order across draws and average in code.

source: Wang et al. (2023) Self-Consistency Improves Chain of Thought Reasoning (ICLR)
finding: Sampling several reasoning paths and marginalising to the final answer by vote beats a single greedy path.
numbers: Gains over greedy chain of thought: GSM8K +17.9, SVAMP +11.0, AQuA +12.2 points.
limits: Vote is a frequency estimate, not a calibrated posterior.
agent_relevance: A vote over draws is the cheap empirical posterior over candidates for S7.

source: Tian et al. (2023) Just Ask for Calibration
finding: For RLHF models, verbalised probabilities are better calibrated than token log-probabilities on TriviaQA, SciQ and TruthfulQA.
numbers: Verbalised confidence cut expected calibration error by a relative 50 percent for ChatGPT, GPT-4 and Claude 2.
limits: Three QA benchmarks. Raw RLHF token probabilities are over-confident.
agent_relevance: Which probability to normalise (verbalised, sampled frequency, logits) must be checked per task class.

source: Kadavath et al. (2022) Language Models (Mostly) Know What They Know
finding: Larger models are well calibrated on multiple-choice and true/false questions when the format is right. P(True) self-evaluation improves when the model sees many of its own samples. P(IK) generalises only partly.
numbers: Calibration improves with model size and few-shot prompting. Replacing an option with 'None of the above' harms performance and calibration (section 3.1). RLHF miscalibration can be fixed by temperature tuning (section 3.3).
limits: Holds on-distribution and with the right format. P(IK) calibration is weak on new tasks.
agent_relevance: Model-stated probabilities may feed a Bayes step, but only after calibration is checked per class.

source: McCoy et al. (2023) Embers of Autoregression
finding: LLM accuracy depends on the probability of the output and the task even when the task is deterministic. A prior-like pull remains in the model.
numbers: GPT-4 decodes a simple cipher with 51 percent accuracy when the output is a high-probability word sequence and 13 percent when low-probability.
limits: Eleven tasks, GPT-3.5 and GPT-4. Only abstract and contents read.
agent_relevance: The model's implicit prior can override evidence when the true answer is unusual.

source: Mandel (2018) coherence of analyst probability forecasts (via repo claims file)
finding: Forcing probabilities over exclusive hypotheses to sum to 1 cut error about 35 percent; averaging many analysts after that cut about 61 percent.
numbers: Repo note: numbers come from Mandel 2018 only; plain normalisation (0.13) did as well as coherentization. Repo status: established.
limits: Human analysts, one task; LLM transfer untested. Only the repo claim text was read, not the paper.
agent_relevance: This is the base of G5. Conditionalization is the update; normalisation is the coherence fix.

source: Binz and Schulz (2022) Using cognitive psychology to understand GPT-3
finding: Only the title page was read. Tests GPT-3 on cognitive psychology tasks.
numbers: Not extracted.
limits: No Bayes-specific numbers collected.
agent_relevance: Candidate for the LLM-focused angle.

source: Griffiths et al. (2023) Bayes in the Age of Intelligent Machines
finding: Title only confirmed. Discusses Bayesian models of cognition and LLMs.
numbers: Not extracted.
limits: Text was not read.
agent_relevance: Candidate for a later pass.

source: Ramsey (1926) Truth and probability; de Finetti (1937) Foresight
finding: Ramsey and de Finetti tie degrees of belief to betting behaviour and show incoherent bets lose for sure.
numbers: Credit taken from SEP (opened); originals not read.

source: Lewis (1999) Why conditionalize?; Teller (1973) Conditionalization and observation
